results.evidence: Opening hook names the fear well ('blue lights hit your mirror and your stomach dropped'), but several H2s are topical rather than action-oriented ('Stage 3: Arraignment — Your First Court Date', 'Stage 4: Discovery — The Evidence Arrives', 'Stage 7: Resolution — How DUI Cases End', 'The 7 Common DUI Defenses — Summary Table').

Legal terms are defined inline on first use ('Reasonable suspicion based on specific, articulable facts', 'Standardized Field Sobriety Tests (SFSTs)', 'NHTSA — the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration'), and paragraphs stay within 4 sentences.

Before the first H2 ('How to Use This Guide'), there is no concrete immediate-action block — only framing text ('Bookmark this page. You're going to need it.'), which is vague rather than a specific under-5-minute action.

Decision points lead with defaults ('You will almost certainly plead not guilty', 'Never accept a plea offer until your attorney has completed every step on this checklist', 'Never plead guilty at arraignment').

Multiple sections exceed 5 unranked items without grouping — the discovery list has 7 bullets ('The police report', 'Dashcam and bodycam footage'...'911 calls or anonymous tips'), the attorney accountability checklist has 8 unranked bullets, and the 'Before You Consider Any Plea Deal' list has 7 unranked items.
This post uses the timeline-post pattern (chronological stages from arrest through resolution with deadlines at each stage).

Scary statistics are paired with actions within 2 sentences — the 18% NHTSA error rate is paired with 'Every deviation from the NHTSA standard is a crack in the prosecution's case', and the 10-day DMV deadline is paired with 'call them today — not tomorrow, today'.

No blame language — the post consistently separates the person from the situation ('The less you understand, the easier you are to process through the system', 'You'll get through this') with no 'you should have' or lecturing patterns.

Opening validates fear well and middle reduces unknown to known, but the post closes with a CTA stack ('Get the DUI Defense Playbook — $97', 'Get your DUI Case Decoder report', 'Take our free case score assessment') and the final sentence 'Know what you're paying for' functions more as a sales close than a pure agency statement.

The 7 Defenses summary table has 4 columns (#, Defense, What It Challenges, Success Indicators) which exceeds the 2-column mobile limit; otherwise headings stay at H2/H3 and sections are reasonably sized.

Most H2 sections have strong bolded screenshot sentences ('A breathalyzer number is not a verdict...', 'The DMV hearing is a free deposition...', 'An attorney who negotiates your plea without watching every second of dashcam footage is negotiating blind'), but Stage 1, Stage 7, and the Defenses Summary Table section lack a single standalone bolded shareable insight.

All four FAQ answers start with direct answers (no preamble), stay within 2-5 sentences, and read naturally ('Not at arraignment, and not before every piece of evidence has been examined', 'Most first-offense DUI cases resolve in 3 to 6 months').
